Gather people and pets Take essential medicines, identification, keys and phone power without delaying departure. Use official routes Smoke and closures can change quickly; do not drive into heavy smoke or flames. Report your destination Tell an out-of-area contact where you are going and follow shelter instructions.

text: Separate an approaching fire from a smoke exposure problem. Keep checking changing wind, fire perimeter, and air-quality conditions. If fire threatens the building or officials order departure, indoor smoke control is no substitute for evacuation. If breathing becomes difficult or symptoms are severe, seek urgent medical help. Create one cleaner-air room using safe filtration if available, reduce indoor smoke sources and avoid strenuous activity. Do not overheat a sealed home; move to a safer breathable and cooler place if you cannot maintain both air quality and safe temperature. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Fire & air Know which problem you face Check official fire, evacuation, and air-quality notices for your address. An evacuation order changes the decision immediately. If sheltering from smoke Close windows and doors. Set HVAC to recirculate where possible, use a portable air cleaner or a cleaner indoor room, and avoid adding indoor smoke from candles, frying, or smoking. Limit outside exposure If you must go outside in smoke, a well-fitting N95 or P100 respirator can reduce particle exposure; ordinary cloth masks do not provide the same protection.
